steps.say: Small kidney tumours are treated while keeping their nephrons. Partial nephrectomy is established as standard for T1a masses of four cm or less. Feasible T1b tumours are also accepted for the same approach. Cancer control is matched to radical removal in studies. Long term renal function is kept better after sparing surgery. Solitary kidneys with bilateral tumours are counted as demanding it.
steps.tx: **Partial nephrectomy** (nephron sparing surgery) is the preferred standard for **T1a masses of 4 cm or less** (under four centimetres) and feasible T1b tumours, matching radical nephrectomy for cancer control while preserving long term renal function. It is mandatory for solitary kidneys, bilateral tumours, and pre existing renal impairment. Plan a clampless or early unclamping technique where anatomy allows, because every spared nephron counts.

vis.alt: Partial nephrectomy excising a small renal tumour with spared parenchyma.
vis.caption: Partial nephrectomy: standard for T1a masses of 4 cm or less. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Clamping the pedicle is viewed as starting an ischaemic clock. Warm ischaemia is advised to stay under twenty to twenty five minutes. Beyond that acute tubular necrosis risk is described as climbing. Cold ischaemia with ice slush is used to buy more time. Thirty five minutes is accepted as the cold limit. Early unclamping is adopted to trim minutes safely.
steps.tx: **Warm ischemia time** (warm ischaemia, clamped kidney minutes) should stay **under 20 to 25 minutes** (below twenty to twenty five) during partial nephrectomy, beyond which **acute tubular necrosis** (tubule death) risk climbs steeply. **Cold ischemia** (cold ischaemia, ice slush cooling) extends the safe window to **under 35 minutes** (below thirty five). Unclamp early after the deep layer and finish the outer layer perfused, because each warm minute injures tubules.

steps.say: Kidney cancer is feared for climbing veins in advanced cases. Four to ten percent are found extending into renal vein and vena cava. The Neves Zincke system is used for staging the thrombus height. Level one is defined as staying in the renal vein. Level two is passed below the liver on scans. Level three is seen reaching inside the liver. Level four is documented crossing the diaphragm.
steps.tx: **IVC thrombus** (vein clot of tumour) complicates **4% to 10%** (four to ten in a hundred) of renal cancers, staged by the **Neves-Zincke classification** (thrombus height scale) from Level I in the renal vein to Level IV above the diaphragm into the atrium. Height sets the surgical plan, from cavotomy to chest opening. Image every large right sided tumour for thrombus, because bland clot and tumour clot need different handling.

vis.alt: Gross specimen of clear cell renal carcinoma with venous extension.
vis.caption: RCC extent: 4 to 10 percent grow thrombus into renal vein and IVC. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Atrial thrombi are managed with a heart lung machine. Level four disease is staged as reaching above the diaphragm. Cardiopulmonary bypass with deep hypothermic arrest is arranged for a bloodless field. Transoesophageal echo is used for tracking the thrombus live. Liver transplant with cardiac teams is joined at the table. This surgery is planned only in expert centres.
steps.tx: **Level IV thrombi** (atrial tumour clot) demand **cardiopulmonary bypass** (heart lung machine) with **deep hypothermic circulatory arrest** (cooled bloodless pause) plus **transoesophageal echocardiography** (food pipe heart ultrasound) monitoring. Cooling stills the circulation so the atrium can be opened and cleared safely. Assemble cardiac, vascular, and urology teams together, because this is among the largest joint operations.

steps.say: Metastatic kidney cancer is sorted by needing risk grouping. The IMDC model is applied using six bedside factors. Karnofsky below eighty percent is counted as one factor. Diagnosis to treatment under one year is added as another. Anaemia with high calcium, high neutrophils, and high platelets is completed as the set. Favourable, intermediate, and poor groups are derived from the total.
steps.tx: **IMDC criteria** (metastatic kidney risk score) sort metastatic clear cell disease with **6 factors** (six counts): Karnofsky performance **below 80%** (under eighty), time from diagnosis to systemic therapy **under 1 year** (below one year), anaemia, **hypercalcaemia** (high calcium), neutrophilia, and thrombocytosis. Zero factors is favourable, one or two intermediate, three or more poor. Risk guides the first line combination, because favourable and poor groups favour different pairings.

steps.say: Intermediate and poor risk disease is started with combinations. Dual immunotherapy is paired as nivolumab with ipilimumab. The alternative is added as a VEGF TKI to PD-1 blockade. Pembrolizumab with axitinib or lenvatinib is listed among proven pairs. Single agent TKI is now rarely kept first. Combination is started before the burden is worsened.
steps.tx: **First line metastatic therapy** (starting drug combination) for intermediate and poor risk clear cell disease pairs **nivolumab plus ipilimumab** (dual checkpoint blockade) or a **VEGFR-TKI plus anti-PD-1/PD-L1** (vessel drug plus immune drug) such as pembrolizumab with axitinib or lenvatinib. Combinations beat single agent TKI on survival, so reserve solo TKI for the unfit or favourable selected cases. Treat at experienced centres, because immune toxicities need conjoint care.

vis.alt: VEGFR tyrosine kinase inhibition combined with checkpoint blockade.
vis.caption: Metastatic combinations: VEGFR-TKI plus PD-1 blockade beats solo TKI. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: High risk disease is feared to recur after nephrectomy. Adjuvant pembrolizumab for one year is prescribed to change the odds. The KEYNOTE five six four trial is cited as proving longer disease free survival. Clear cell histology with high risk features is selected as qualifying. Thyroid with bowel, lung, and liver is monitored on therapy. Therapy is stopped early for severe immune toxicity.
steps.tx: **Adjuvant pembrolizumab** (preventive immune drug) for **1 year** (one year) after nephrectomy prolongs disease free survival in resected high risk clear cell carcinoma, proven by the **KEYNOTE-564** (pembro prevention trial). Select tumours with high grade, large size, nodal disease, or resected metastases. Watch thyroid, colon, lung, and liver for immune attack each visit, because early steroid rescue preserves benefit.

vis.alt: Organ systems affected by checkpoint inhibitor toxicity.
vis.caption: Adjuvant pembrolizumab: watch thyroid bowel lung and liver each visit. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Not every small mass is sent for the knife. Tumours under three cm in frail comorbid patients are judged suited to watching. Thermal ablation is offered as a middle path forward. Cryoablation is used for freezing and radiofrequency for heating the lesion. Repeat imaging is arranged for tracking growth rate. Intervention for clear growth or young fit patients is advised.
steps.tx: **Active surveillance** (watched waiting) or **thermal ablation** (cryoablation freezing or **radiofrequency ablation** (needle heating)) suits **small masses under 3 cm** (below three centimetres) in elderly comorbid patients unfit for surgery. Track size with serial cross sectional imaging and biopsy uncertain lesions. Convert to surgery or ablation on growth, because youth and fitness favour definitive cure.
